note: Zone lore for the Journal page. Written for WoW Oracle (short summaries in our own words). 'featured' are quest titles (first quest of a chain) that should always be among the tales; the rest are found from the quest data.

zones.summary: The green heartland of Stormwind, all farms, vineyards and quiet woods. Under the calm, the kingdom is stretched thin: kobolds dig in the old mines, gnolls raid from the Redridge border, and the Defias Brotherhood recruits among the people the crown forgot. Northshire Abbey, where many heroes take their first steps, still guards the valley.

Snowbound valleys around the mountain city of Ironforge, home of the dwarves and their gnome allies. Since Gnomeregan was lost to the troggs and its own radiation, refugee gnomes share Kharanos with dwarven brewers and mountaineers. Frostmane trolls hold the high caves, and Dark Iron agents are never as far away as anyone would like.

The new World Tree, planted by Archdruid Fandral Staghelm without the blessing of the dragons. The night elves live in its branches, but something is wrong in Teldrassil: the wildlife grows aggressive, the furbolgs have turned on old friends, and a corruption creeps through the glades that the druids prefer not to name.

A harsh red land named for Thrall's father, Durotan, and given to the orcs after they crossed the sea. Orgrimmar rises from its canyons. The Horde has enemies close to home here: the Burning Blade cult whispering of demons, Kul Tiran marines at Tiragarde Keep, and the restless centaur and harpies on every border.

Rolling grasslands where the tauren settled at last under Cairne Bloodhoof, with Thunder Bluff on its mesas. The Earth Mother's land is peaceful but not safe: the Grimtotem clan schemes against Cairne, gnolls dig in the Venture Co. mines, and the centaur raid from the Barrens.

Once the farmland of Lordaeron, now a grey country of dead fields above the ruined capital. The Forsaken, undead freed from the Lich King's will, have made the Undercity their home under Sylvanas Windrunner. Their apothecaries work on a new plague of their own, while the Scarlet Crusade hunts every undead thing from its monastery in the north.

Stormwind's breadbasket, abandoned by the kingdom it fed. When the crown refused to pay the stonemasons who rebuilt the capital, Edwin VanCleef led them into the shadows as the Defias Brotherhood. Now harvest golems turn on the farmers, the People's Militia stands almost alone at Sentinel Hill, and the Brotherhood hides something big beneath Moonbrook.

A lake valley held behind the great Stonewrought Dam, with the dwarven town of Thelsamar on its shore. The Explorers' League digs for the past at Ironband's Excavation, troggs spill out of the earth, and Dark Iron dwarves have set their eyes on the dam itself.

A misty coast where the night elves once had cities, now ruins half swallowed by the sea. From Auberdine, sentinels watch the shattered towers of the Highborne, where satyrs and demon-touched cultists gather. The wildlife is sick, the furbolgs are changing, and the old towers still hold secrets from before the Sundering.

An endless savanna crossed by caravans, centaur raiders and goblin traders. At Crossroads the Horde holds the middle, while Ratchet trades with anyone. The druids of the Fang dreamed of making the Barrens green again; their nightmare now twists the Wailing Caverns. Beneath the plains, the quilboar of Razorfen hold their thorny strongholds.

Dark pine woods on the edge of the old kingdom of Gilneas, whose great wall keeps the world out. The Forsaken push south from the Sepulcher. Worgen howl in the night, and the shattered keep of Shadowfang holds the mad archmage Arugal and the curse he unleashed.

Red stone hills around Lakeshire, a town that has been begging Stormwind for help for a long time. The Blackrock orcs who once served the Old Horde have come down from the mountains to the north, gnolls fill the valleys, and the bridge and the town barely hold.

A high wilderness sacred to the druids, where the Stonetalon Peak looks over everything. The Venture Co. cuts the ancient forests with shredders, the Charred Vale still smokes, and the Grimtotem and the Horde quarrel over the land the goblins have not yet taken.

The great forest of the night elves and the oldest battlefield between them and the orcs. Here Grom Hellscream killed the demigod Cenarius, and the Warsong clan still cuts the trees. Satyrs haunt the corrupted groves, and the ruins of night elf temples lie quiet among the ancient trees.

Once the bright Brightwood Grove, now a forest of permanent night. Darkshire's Night Watch stands against the undead of Raven Hill, the worgen in the woods and the necromancers in the hills. Old murders are not forgotten here: the town remembers Stalvan Mistmantle, and Sven still wants revenge for his family.

A drowned land between the dwarves and the north. Menethil Harbor is the Alliance's door to Kalimdor and Northrend, while Grim Batol, the dark mountain where the orcs once held the Red Dragonqueen captive, looms in the east. The Dragonmaw orcs and the Dark Irons both fight for the old fortresses.

Farms and fields below Alterac, where Southshore and Tarren Mill face each other over a fragile border. Durnholde Keep is where Thrall grew up as a gladiator and slave before he freed his people. The Forsaken work on new poisons here, and Hillsbrad suffers between the two factions.

A canyon of stone pillars and the dry salt flats of the Shimmering Flats, where goblins and gnomes race their rocket cars. The tauren of Freewind Post live on the mesa tops, while the Galak centaur and Grimtotem raid below.

The ruined kingdom of Alterac, betrayed by its own king Aiden Perenolde, who sided with the Horde in the Second War. Ogres hold the ruined capital, the Syndicate gathers the old nobility's scheming heirs, and the Dalaran crater shows where the mages sealed their city away.

The cradle of humankind: here stood Strom, capital of the ancient Arathor empire that first allied with the high elves against the trolls. Stromgarde is now a broken city held by a few loyal soldiers, Hammerfall is an orc stronghold, and the Witherbark trolls remember an old war.

A grey, dying land of bones, where the centaur clans war among themselves and the Burning Legion's servants linger. The tomb of Zaetar, the son of Cenarius and father of the centaur, lies under the caves of Maraudon, where his consort, the earth princess Theradras, still rules.

A huge jungle that was once the heart of the Gurubashi troll empire. Its ruins lie everywhere, and the blood god Hakkar stirs in Zul'Gurub. Pirates rule the coast from Booty Bay, Hemet Nesingwary hunts everything that moves, and Kurzen's rebels hide deep in the trees.

Swamp land around Theramore, the city Jaina Proudmoore founded to keep the peace between humans and orcs. Not everyone agrees: deserters from the Alliance, black dragonspawn in the south and Onyxia herself, hidden in her lair, all play their part.

A dead, sunburnt land of canyons and dragon bones, scorched in the Second War. The Explorers' League is drawn here by Uldaman, a titan vault older than the dwarves, and what they find there may change what the dwarves believe about their own origins.

A drowned swamp that hides the Sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar, where the Atal'ai trolls tried to summon the blood god and were sunk beneath the water by the green dragonflight. The dragons still guard the temple, and the trolls still worship.

A rainforest of giant trees on Kalimdor's west coast. In the ruins of Eldre'Thalas, now called Dire Maul, Highborne survivors still feed on a captured demon, while ogres hold the outer halls. The green dragons guard one of the portals to the Emerald Dream.

Wild hills where the Wildhammer dwarves fly their gryphons from Aerie Peak. The Revantusk trolls are friendly to the Horde, but the Witherbark and Vilebranch trolls in Jintha'Alor still worship old loa, and a green dragon portal lies hidden in the Seradane.

A golden desert around the goblin town of Gadgetzan. Zul'Farrak's sand trolls guard their city, the Caverns of Time are hidden in the east under the bronze dragonflight's watch, and the Sandfury and Wastewander bandits make every water source a battlefield.

A scorched wound in the mountains, created when the Dark Iron sorcerer-king Thaurissan summoned Ragnaros the Firelord. Dark Iron slaves dig at the Cauldron, and the gate to Blackrock Mountain stands open. Thorium Brotherhood smiths work here, not quite on any side.

An autumn coast named for the queen who brought the Burning Legion into the world. Ruins of her Highborne palaces lie everywhere, naga swim the shores, and the blue dragon Azuregos guards something only he understands.
Red, broken land around the Dark Portal, where the orcs first came into Azeroth. Demons still slip through, and the Nethergarde Keep mages watch the portal day and night.

A sunken jungle of dinosaurs, glowing crystals and steaming vents. The crater is a garden of the titans, and its pylons and crystals hold power that a few scholars at Marshal's Refuge are only beginning to understand.

A northern forest poisoned by the Burning Legion during the Third War. Demon fel moss and corrupted moonwells drip everywhere, and the satyrs of Jaedenar serve the shadow. The Cenarion Circle tries to heal the trees; the Emerald Sanctuary is one of the last green places.

An ash-choked plain around Blackrock Mountain, where the Blackrock orcs serve Nefarian's black dragonflight. Under the mountain the Dark Iron dwarves serve Ragnaros. Between them lie the bones of the Second War and the smoke of both.

Lordaeron's heartland, now a sick land where farms rot under the Scourge. Andorhal's ruins show where the plague first spread through grain, Hearthglen belongs to the Scarlet Crusade, and the necromancers study in Scholomance beneath Caer Darrow.

zones.summary: The worst of the Scourge's land, around the dead city of Stratholme that Arthas purged. The Argent Dawn holds Light's Hope Chapel, where the Light once broke the undead, and the ghosts of Darrowshire still fight a battle they lost long ago.

A snowy valley in the far north of Kalimdor, guarded by the night elves of Starfall Village and the goblins of Everlook. The Winterfall furbolgs are poisoned with corrupted firewater, and the blue dragons of Mazthoril watch over secrets of the ancient night elves.

A desert of insect hives at the southern edge of Kalimdor. Behind the Scarab Wall, sealed a thousand years ago in the War of the Shifting Sands, the qiraji and their old god master wait in Ahn'Qiraj. The Cenarion Circle watches from Cenarion Hold, and the Twilight's Hammer gathers in the dunes.
A lifeless valley around Karazhan, the tower of the Guardian Medivh, who opened the Dark Portal. Nothing grows here and the ghosts of the tower still walk the paths.
A peaceful sanctuary of the druids, where Malfurion Stormrage once taught. All druids, of any race, may come here, and the Cenarion Circle keeps the peace.

The great human capital, rebuilt after the First War with the stonemasons' work. The young King Anduin Wrynn rules in the absence of his father, who disappeared on a diplomatic journey; Lady Katrana Prestor advises the court, and not everyone trusts her.

The dwarven city carved deep in the mountain, ruled by King Magni Bronzebeard. The Explorers' League keeps its halls full of discovered treasures, and the king's daughter Moira has been taken by the Dark Irons.
The night elf city in the branches of Teldrassil, under High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind and Fandral Staghelm. The Temple of the Moon holds the priestesses of Elune.
Thrall's capital, built in Durotar's canyons and named for his mentor Orgrim Doomhammer. The Warchief's hall stands at the heart of the city, and the Horde gathers here before every campaign.
The tauren city on the mesas of Mulgore, joined by rope bridges. Cairne Bloodhoof leads from here, and the Elder Rise holds the druids and shamans who speak for the Earth Mother.

The sewers and crypts beneath ruined Lordaeron, now home to the Forsaken. Queen Sylvanas Windrunner rules from the Royal Quarter, and the Royal Apothecary Society works on things it would rather not talk about.
